h1: Ranch Entrance Gates in Waco, TX: Custom Steel, Stone Columns, and Cattle Guards
heroSub: Your entrance is the first thing anybody sees when they pull up to your place. We build ranch entrances around Waco and Central Texas that look sharp, swing true, and hold up for decades.
introHtml:
If you're looking for ranch entrance gates in Waco, TX, you've probably driven past a hundred entrances and noticed the difference between the ones done right and the ones sagging off a bent T-post. A proper entrance starts with heavy steel, deep concrete footings, and posts sized for the gate they carry. Brazos Ridge Fence Co. builds custom entrances across McLennan, Bosque, and Falls counties, from a clean 16-foot steel swing gate to a full limestone-column entrance with an overhead arch and your ranch name cut in steel.

Most of our custom entrances run $5,000 to $25,000 and up depending on gate width, stonework, and automation. We also install cattle guards, automatic gate operators, and solar power setups for entrances a mile off the nearest meter. Every job starts with a free written estimate, and every price is in writing before we dig the first hole. Call us at (254) 555-0184 and we'll come walk your entrance with you.

sections.heading: Custom Steel and Stone Entrances Built for Central Texas
sections.html:
A ranch entrance has one job on top of looking good: it has to work every single day. That means gate posts heavy enough for the load, usually 6 to 8 inch pipe set 4 feet deep in concrete, and hinges that carry a 20-foot steel gate without sagging by next summer. We build entrances the same way we build our pipe fence, with drill stem and heavy-wall pipe that shrugs off cattle, weather, and time.

On the custom side, most projects land between $5,000 and $25,000 or more. A straightforward steel entrance with a wide swing gate and pipe wings starts near the bottom of that range. Add limestone columns, an overhead arch with your ranch name, decorative steel panels, and automation, and you're at the top end or past it. We'll price out two or three options so you can see exactly where the money goes.

Every entrance ties into the fence around it. We match your entrance to existing barbed wire, pipe, or game fence so the whole frontage reads as one piece instead of a fancy gate bolted onto a tired fence line.

sections.heading: Automatic Gate Operators That Actually Hold Up
sections.html:
Getting out of the truck in the rain to drag a gate open gets old fast. We install automatic gate operators built for heavy steel ranch gates, not the light-duty units made for a suburban driveway. Most operator packages add $2,500 to $6,000 to an entrance depending on gate weight, access controls, and power.

You've got options for how it opens:

  • Remotes and keypads: clickers for the family trucks, a keypad code for the feed delivery and the vet.
  • Phone and intercom access: buzz visitors in from the house or from town.
  • Exit sensors: the gate opens on its own when you drive up from the inside.
  • Solar power: a panel and deep-cycle battery run the operator where there's no line power for a mile.

We size the operator to the gate, set it up, and show you how everything works before we leave. If a storm knocks something loose later, our 24/7 emergency line is (254) 555-0184.

sections.heading: Cattle Guards: Drive Through, Cattle Stay Put
sections.html:
A cattle guard is the best money you'll spend on a working entrance. No stopping, no gate to swing, and no chance somebody leaves it open with 40 head of cattle on the wrong side of it. We install steel cattle guards on poured concrete foundations for $3,500 to $8,000 installed, depending on width and load rating.

The install matters as much as the guard itself. We excavate the pit, form and pour the footings, set the guard level with the road, and finish the approaches so you're not bottoming out a trailer every time you cross. For entrances that see heavy equipment, we spec guards rated for loaded trucks and trailers, not just pickups.

Plenty of our customers pair a cattle guard with a swing gate beside it, so livestock trailers and equipment use the gate and everything else rolls straight through. If you're planning a bigger fencing project around the entrance, our ranch fence cost guide breaks down real per-foot numbers for the whole job.

sections.heading: What a Real Entrance Does for Your Property's Value
sections.html:
Ask any land broker in Central Texas what buyers notice first and they'll tell you: the entrance. A custom steel and limestone entrance sets the tone for the whole property before anybody sees the house, the barn, or the pasture. On ranch and recreational land around Waco, a well-built entrance is one of the few improvements that shows up in the listing photos and in the appraisal.

It's not just resale either. Your entrance is what you drive through every day and what your name hangs over. A gate that opens smooth, columns that stand plumb, and a fence line that runs straight say something about how the rest of the place is run.

We build ranch entrances throughout McLennan, Bosque, and Falls counties, including China Spring, Crawford, McGregor, Valley Mills, Lorena, and West. Call (254) 555-0184 for a free written estimate and we'll meet you at the gate.

faq.q: How much does a ranch entrance gate cost in Waco, TX?
faq.a: Most custom entrances we build run $5,000 to $25,000 and up. A steel swing gate on heavy pipe posts with short wings starts around $5,000 to $8,000. Limestone columns, an overhead arch with your ranch name, and an automatic operator push the project to $15,000 to $25,000 or more. Every job gets a free written estimate with the exact number before we start.

faq.q: How much does a cattle guard cost installed?
faq.a: We install steel cattle guards for $3,500 to $8,000 depending on width and load rating. A standard 8-foot-deep guard spanning a 14 to 16 foot entrance with a concrete foundation sits near the middle of that range. Guards rated for loaded semis and heavy equipment cost more than pickup-rated units. That price includes excavation, concrete footings, the guard, and finished approaches.

faq.q: How much does it cost to add an automatic gate opener?
faq.a: Plan on $2,500 to $6,000 on top of the entrance itself. The low end covers a single commercial operator with remotes on a gate near line power. Dual-swing gates, keypads, phone access, and solar power for remote entrances move you toward the high end. We only install operators rated for the actual weight of your gate, which is why they last.

faq.q: How long does it take to build a custom ranch entrance?
faq.a: A basic steel entrance usually takes 2 to 4 days on site once materials are in hand. Entrances with limestone columns need 1 to 2 weeks because masonry and concrete need cure time before the gates hang. Custom plasma-cut signage and arches can add a week or two of shop time up front. We'll give you a schedule in writing with your estimate.

faq.q: Can you match my new entrance to my existing fence?
faq.a: Yes, and we'd argue you should. We tie new entrances into existing barbed wire, pipe, and high game fence so the frontage looks like one build instead of two. If the fence on either side of the entrance is rough, we can quote replacing the first few hundred feet at the same time, which usually saves money over a separate trip. Most frontage fence runs $12 to $35 per foot depending on the type.
